sections.html:
You can sell for cash, list with an agent or sell it yourself. A cash buyer shortens the timeline because there is no loan approval and no appraisal gap to worry about.

Listing may bring more money from a financed buyer, though showings, inspection requests and a lender's schedule stretch the process. A house with an aging roof, code problems or an estate attached often moves better to a direct buyer. A well kept house with time on the clock deserves a listing opinion alongside any cash offer.

  • Line up each offer by closing date and the cash you would walk away with.
  • Ask who covers title charges and deed tax.
  • Verify that no lien or tax balance will block the deed.

sections.h2: About Largo and its older houses
sections.html:
Largo was incorporated in 1905 and grew fast after a freeze in 1962 pushed grove owners to sell land to builders. The city now has over 80,000 residents, so much of the housing dates from the postwar and post-freeze building years, with a few older pockets from the citrus era such as Dansville, which began with a 1946 purchase of 80 acres in southwest Largo.

Keep your build year and upgrade receipts handy. A buyer's inspector will ask for the roof date and the age of the air conditioner and the electrical panel. The Largo Public Library and the Pinellas County Historic Preservation Board are places to look for photographs or permit history on an old house.

Bills go out on the last business day of October, payments are accepted from November 1, and April 1 starts delinquency. The Pinellas County Property Appraiser sets values, and the tax collector mails and collects the bills. Up to two owners print on a bill, and address changes go through the appraiser, not the collector. If your mortgage company escrows your taxes, the notice you receive may be informational only.

For the 2026 bills the tax certificate sale is May 28, 2027. Besides paying in full, the collector offers an installment plan for estimated bills over $100, with applications from November 1 through April 30. A partial payment plan takes payments of $100 or more but forfeits early discounts, and homestead owners may apply to defer taxes by March 31, which creates a lien and accrues interest.

Pinellas payment options from the tax collector
Payment optionTerms
Early paymentDiscount period November through February
Installment planFour payments, bill over $100, enroll November 1 to April 30
Partial payments$100 minimum, ends March 31, discounts forfeited
DeferralHomestead owners, lien and interest apply

sections.h2: What happens when a Largo tax bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
The sequence can end in a tax deed auction. After April 1 interest and costs are added, and Florida law prohibits partial payments of delinquent real estate taxes.

By June 1 the collector sells a tax certificate on the parcel, awarded to the bidder who accepts the lowest interest, with unsold certificates struck off to the county at 18 percent. After two years the holder can start a tax deed application. The collector mails a warning letter each February to owners at risk, with a deadline of the last business day of March.

Once a deed action begins, all outstanding taxes roll into a single amount plus interest and costs, and only full payment stops it. Personal checks are not accepted for tax deed payments, only cash, wire or certified funds. If any part of your bill is behind, call the Pinellas County Tax Collector before you list and get a written payoff.

sections.h2: Deed tax, recording and short-term rental taxes
sections.html:
The deed carries Florida's 70 cents per $100 documentary stamp tax, collected by the clerk at recording. Quitclaim deeds, deeds in lieu of foreclosure and contracts for deed are on the taxable list, so a family transfer for value is not automatically exempt. A mortgage on the property counts as consideration. Recording is $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, and two witnesses must see the deed signed.

If you have rented the house to short-term guests, the Pinellas tax collector describes a 6 percent tourist development tax on stays of six months or less, with a 7 percent state sales tax on top for a total of 13 percent. Returns are due even when no rent was collected, and a late return carries a $50 minimum penalty. Settle those accounts before you close.

  • Close or update your tourist tax account if you rent short term.
  • Collect lease copies for long-term tenants.
  • Ask the title company what it needs for the deed.

Tenants and estates both add timelines. Pinellas taxes furniture and equipment in rental properties as tangible personal property, billed to whoever owns it on January 1, and any unpaid lien on it survives a sale of the property. Check that those accounts are paid.

A year-to-year tenancy ends on 60 days' notice, a quarter-to-quarter one on 30 and a week-to-week one on 7. A sheriff posts 24 hours' notice before returning possession after a court judgment.

For an estate, Florida has had no state estate tax for people who died after 2004, and the personal representative no longer files the state forms. The heirs still need someone with court authority to sign the deed, so ask a probate attorney or the clerk what the title company will require.

A typical cash sale starts with an offer and a signed contract. The title company then searches for mortgages, liens and tax balances. You review a settlement statement that shows the payoff, deed tax, recording and any prorated taxes, and then you sign the deed in front of two witnesses.

Bring photo ID, the payoff letter from your lender, your latest tax bill and any lease copies. If a tourist tax or personal property account exists, close it out in the weeks before settlement. After the deed is recorded, the closing agent sends you the balance of the proceeds.

Ask each buyer to state in writing the deposit, the closing date and who pays each fee. Two or three written offers on the same lines are easy to compare, and weak offers stand out fast.

sections.h2: Checklist before you list in Largo
sections.html:
Largo buyers, especially investors, usually want to know three things first: what the roof and air conditioning look like, whether the taxes are current, and whether the property carries any rental accounts with the county. Having those answers on one sheet speeds every conversation.

  • Roof, air conditioner and electrical panel dates, with receipts.
  • This year's tax bill and proof of payment, or a payoff figure from the tax collector.
  • Copies of any lease, plus a note on whether the tenant will stay or leave.
  • Names of every person on the deed, since each must be available to sign.

If a relative lives out of state, plan the signing early. Mobile notaries and the title company can often arrange a remote signing, but two witnesses are still required for the deed.

faqs.a: Pinellas County. The Pinellas County Property Appraiser sets values and the Pinellas County Tax Collector mails the bills.

faqs.q: When do Pinellas tax bills go out?
faqs.a: On the last business day of October, and payment is accepted from November 1. April 1 is the delinquency date.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Largo tax bill by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes, online, with a 2.50 percent convenience fee from the payment processor. eChecks are free. Delinquent taxes cannot be paid by personal check.

faqs.q: What stops a tax deed process?
faqs.a: Full payment of the rolled-up amount, with interest and costs, in cash, wire or certified funds. Installments do not stop it once the action has started.

faqs.q: What is Largo's tourist tax if I rented the house?
faqs.a: It is a 6 percent tourist development tax on rentals of six months or less, plus 7 percent sales tax. Ask the Pinellas tax collector to close the account when you sell.
